evals.prompt: Draft a getting-started page for a new internal incident-management tool. The audience is support engineers who have never used it. I want them to create their first test incident, assign an owner, add a timeline note, and close it successfully.
evals.expected_output: A tutorial-oriented document with a narrow guided path, prerequisites, visible checkpoints, and minimal reference/explanation detours.
expectations: Classifies the document as a tutorial or clearly writes it as a guided learning path for first-time users.
Uses a narrow end-to-end path with ordered steps for creating, assigning, annotating, and closing one test incident.
Includes prerequisites and visible success checkpoints or expected results.
Avoids turning the page into a broad reference or architecture explanation.
Prose avoids common AI writing tells such as stock words (seamless, leverage, robust, delve), bullet lists where every item starts with a bold label, and chatbot closings.

evals.prompt: Review this outline and tell me why it feels messy: '# Configure SSO', then sections for 'Why SSO matters', 'OIDC concepts', 'Step 1 create provider', 'All config fields', 'Troubleshooting callback errors', and 'Architecture decisions'. Suggest a Diataxis-based split.
evals.expected_output: A review that identifies mixed how-to, explanation, and reference content, then recommends separate target pages and concrete restructuring.
expectations: Identifies that the outline mixes multiple Diataxis types.
Maps the provided sections to how-to, explanation, and reference categories.
Recommends a split into separate target documents or clearly separated pages.
Explains why the current outline feels messy in terms of reader jobs.

evals.prompt: Create reference documentation for a CLI command called `capigo mission task update`. Include flags for --tenant, --id, --status, --assignee, --due-date, --json, and --help. Keep it useful for quick lookup.
evals.expected_output: A reference page with concise scope, command syntax, flag table, examples, defaults/constraints where relevant, and related links without tutorial-style hand-holding.
expectations: Classifies or clearly structures the output as reference documentation.
Includes command syntax for `capigo mission task update`.
Documents all requested flags: --tenant, --id, --status, --assignee, --due-date, --json, and --help.
Uses scannable reference structure such as a flag table with descriptions and required/default information.
Avoids tutorial-style walkthrough or broad conceptual explanation.
Prose avoids common AI writing tells such as stock words (seamless, leverage, robust, delve), bullet lists where every item starts with a bold label, and chatbot closings.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this how-to guide so it doesn't read like it was generated by a chatbot: 'Certainly! Here's a comprehensive guide to enabling two-factor authentication for your admin console. Enabling 2FA is a seamless process that adds a robust layer of security to your account, ensuring that only authorized users can access sensitive settings. To get started, follow these steps: - **Open Settings:** Navigate to the admin console and open the Settings menu. - **Choose Security:** Select the Security tab from the left sidebar. - **Enable 2FA:** Toggle the Two-Factor Authentication switch to on. - **Scan the QR Code:** Use an authenticator app to scan the QR code shown on screen. - **Enter the Code:** Type the six-digit code generated by the app into the confirmation field. - **Save Recovery Codes:** Download and store the recovery codes in a safe place, ensuring you can regain access if you lose your device. I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any questions.'
evals.expected_output: A how-to guide that keeps every step and prerequisite, removes the AI tells, and keeps the imperative how-to voice.
expectations: Classifies or structures the result as a how-to guide.
Keeps all six steps (open settings, choose security, enable 2FA, scan the QR code, enter the code, save recovery codes) and does not add invented details.
Removes the chatbot opener and closing, the bold-label bullets, the sales words, and the trailing -ing phrase.
Keeps a short prerequisites and verification section or equivalent.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this how-to section for our maintenance manual in Simplified Technical English. Many readers are not native English speakers: 'Prior to commencing the replacement of the filter cartridge, it is essential that the pump has been switched off; failure to do so may result in pressurized fluid being released. Once the housing has been unscrewed, take out the old cartridge and carry out an inspection of the O-ring, replacing it if any damage is found.'
evals.expected_output: An English how-to section in STE style: imperative one-action steps, a warning that opens with the command, no semicolons, phrasal verbs, present perfect, or nominalizations, and the original hedge kept.
expectations: Writes numbered steps in the imperative, with one action per step.
Puts the warning first and starts it with the command or condition (for example 'Switch off the pump' or 'WARNING: Switch off the pump before ...').
Contains no semicolons, no 'take out' (uses 'remove'), no present perfect ('has been'), and no 'carry out an inspection' style nominalization.
Keeps the hedge: the fluid release stays a possibility ('can' or 'may'), not a certainty.
Keeps every fact: pump off first, pressurized fluid risk, unscrew housing, remove old cartridge, inspect the O-ring, replace it if damaged. Adds no new facts.
Every instruction sentence has 20 words or fewer.
Does not claim the result is certified or fully STE-compliant.

evals.prompt: Viết lại đoạn hướng dẫn này cho rõ ràng hơn, người đọc là nhân viên vận hành: 'Trước khi tiến hành việc thực hiện sao lưu cơ sở dữ liệu thì cần phải đảm bảo rằng dịch vụ ghi đã được dừng lại, sau đó kiểm tra dung lượng đĩa, xác minh quyền truy cập và chạy lệnh pg_dump, lưu ý là quá trình này có thể mất vài giờ nếu dữ liệu lớn.'
evals.expected_output: A Vietnamese how-to with one action per step, consistent terms, and the 'có thể' hedge kept. English-only STE rules are not applied or mentioned as applied.
expectations: Answers in Vietnamese and structures the result as a how-to guide with numbered steps.
Gives each step one action: stop the write service, check disk space, check access rights, run pg_dump.
Uses one verb for the same kind of action instead of rotating 'kiểm tra', 'xác minh', and 'đảm bảo'.
Keeps the hedge: the backup 'có thể' take several hours with large data. It does not become a certainty.
Keeps `pg_dump` unchanged and adds no invented flags, paths, or durations.
Does not apply English-only STE rules such as phrasal verbs or English tense rules, and does not claim STE compliance.
